es: Identificar seis recursos retóricos en un discurso escolar y explicar qué efecto buscan en el público.

vocabulary.es: regla de tres: tres elementos seguidos
imagen vívida, que se ve con claridad

teaching.en: We need books, we need quiet, and we need a place to belong; by the third demand, the audience can feel a steady rhythm in the speech.
teaching.es: Necesitamos libros, necesitamos silencio y necesitamos un lugar al que pertenecer; a la tercera demanda, el público ya siente un ritmo constante en el discurso.
teaching.explanationEs: Rule of three: tres elementos con la misma forma dan ritmo y dejan la idea completa.
segments: We need books, we need quiet, and we need a place to belong; by
the third demand, the audience can feel a steady rhythm in the speech.
teaching.audioText: We need books, we need quiet, and we need a place to belong; by the third demand, the audience can feel a steady rhythm in the speech.

teaching.en: Who will speak for this library when the doors are closed, the shelves are empty and nobody is left to ask why?
teaching.es: ¿Quién hablará por esta biblioteca cuando las puertas estén cerradas, los estantes vacíos y no quede nadie que pregunte por qué?
teaching.explanationEs: Rhetorical question: nadie responde en voz alta; el público piensa y se implica.
segments: Who will speak for this library when the doors are closed,
the shelves are empty and nobody is left to ask why?
teaching.audioText: Who will speak for this library when the doors are closed, the shelves are empty and nobody is left to ask why?

teaching.en: Some people see a row of old shelves, but we see a stark contrast between what this school promises and what it offers.
teaching.es: Algunos ven una fila de estantes viejos, pero nosotros vemos un contraste marcado entre lo que esta escuela promete y lo que ofrece.
teaching.explanationEs: Stark contrast: dos visiones opuestas puestas una junto a otra hacen más fuerte la tuya.
segments: Some people see a row of old shelves, but we see a
stark contrast between what this school promises and what it offers.
teaching.audioText: Some people see a row of old shelves, but we see a stark contrast between what this school promises and what it offers.

teaching.en: We will not remain silent, we will not step back, and we will not let this library close without a fight.
teaching.es: No permaneceremos callados, no retrocederemos y no dejaremos que esta biblioteca cierre sin luchar.
teaching.explanationEs: Repetition: repetir el comienzo de cada frase da fuerza y hace que la idea se recuerde.
segments: We will not remain silent, we will not step back, and
we will not let this library close without a fight.
teaching.audioText: We will not remain silent, we will not step back, and we will not let this library close without a fight.

teaching.en: Imagine a child in a dark corridor, holding a book like a lantern, and reflect for a moment on what that small light is worth.
teaching.es: Imagina a un niño en un pasillo oscuro, sosteniendo un libro como un farol, y reflexiona un momento sobre lo que vale esa pequeña luz.
teaching.explanationEs: Vivid image: una imagen concreta hace que el público vea la idea, no solo que la entienda.
segments: Imagine a child in a dark corridor, holding a book like a lantern,
and reflect for a moment on what that small light is worth.
teaching.audioText: Imagine a child in a dark corridor, holding a book like a lantern, and reflect for a moment on what that small light is worth.

teaching.en: You, the people sitting in this hall tonight, are the only voice this library has, so the decision belongs to you.
teaching.es: Ustedes, las personas sentadas en esta sala esta noche, son la única voz que tiene esta biblioteca; la decisión les pertenece.
teaching.explanationEs: Apelación directa: you habla al público y lo convierte en protagonista del mensaje.
segments: You, the people sitting in this hall tonight, are the only
voice this library has, so the decision belongs to you.
teaching.audioText: You, the people sitting in this hall tonight, are the only voice this library has, so the decision belongs to you.

prompt.es: Identifica el recurso retórico de la frase y su efecto.

choices.text: Repetition: one phrase returns to keep the idea fixed in the audience's mind.
Rule of three: three matching demands give the sentence a steady beat.
Stark contrast: two opposite views make the speaker's side look stronger.

feedback.es: Los estantes viejos y el único lugar donde todo niño puede leer se oponen: un contraste que realza la postura del orador.

hint.es: Fíjate en cuántas miradas distintas aparecen y cómo se oponen.

origin.text: “Some people see a row of old shelves; we see the only place in this town where every child can sit down and read for free.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Una pregunta retórica busca que el público piense, no que responda.»

feedback.es: Una pregunta retórica se formula para provocar reflexión, no para recibir respuesta: por eso la oradora deja trabajar al silencio.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que sigue a «rhetorical».

origin.text: She did not wait for an answer. She asked, “Who will speak for this library?” and let the silence do the rest. A rhetorical ___ is meant to make listeners think, not reply.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Donde el ayuntamiento ve un gasto, nosotros vemos un futuro.»

answer.text: Where the council sees a cost, we see a future

feedback.es: El contraste opone dos miradas: la del ayuntamiento y la de we, con la misma estructura en las dos mitades.

hint.es: Primero va la visión del ayuntamiento y después la de we.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige el recurso de las tres frases antes de la imagen final.

choices.text: A repeated opening phrase that makes the speaker sound determined.
A list of three needs that gives the speech a steady beat.
A pair of opposite views that makes the speaker's side stronger.

feedback.es: We will not aparece al inicio de tres frases seguidas: es repetición, que transmite decisión y deja la idea clavada.

origin.audio: At the school assembly, the head of the student council got up and spoke without notes. We need books, we need quiet, and we need a place to belong. Some people see old shelves; we see the last place where every child is welcome. Who will speak for this library when the doors are closed? We will not remain silent. We will not step back. We will not let it close. Imagine a child in the dark, holding a book like a lantern.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del discurso con el efecto que busca.

pairs: Not one more delay. Not one more excuse.

pairs.es: repetición: insiste hasta que la idea se queda

pairs: Some see a cost; we see a future.

pairs.es: contraste: opone dos miradas para destacar la tuya

pairs: Imagine a child holding a book like a lantern.

pairs.es: imagen vívida: el público ve la escena

pairs: You are the only voice this library has.

pairs.es: apelación directa: el público es protagonista

feedback.es: Cada recurso cumple una función distinta: insistir, oponer, hacer ver o implicar al público.

pairs: Not one more delay. Not one more excuse.

pairs.es: repetición: insiste hasta que la idea se queda

pairs: Some see a cost; we see a future.

pairs.es: contraste: opone dos miradas para destacar la tuya

pairs: Imagine a child holding a book like a lantern.

pairs.es: imagen vívida: el público ve la escena

pairs: You are the only voice this library has.

prompt.es: Con el mismo fragmento, ¿qué deja entender la oradora sobre el cierre de la biblioteca?

choices.text: That the council has decided and speaking up is useless now.
That the closure is not final and the audience can still prevent it.
That the library will close because students stopped reading.
That the audience should wait for the council's decision before acting.

feedback.es: «We will not let it close» y la pregunta sobre quién hablará dan a entender que aún se puede evitar el cierre, si el público actúa.

origin.audio: At the school assembly, the head of the student council got up and spoke without notes. We need books, we need quiet, and we need a place to belong. Some people see old shelves; we see the last place where every child is welcome. Who will speak for this library when the doors are closed? We will not remain silent. We will not step back. We will not let it close. Imagine a child in the dark, holding a book like a lantern.

prompt.es: Escucha el informe y elige con qué propósito empezó la alumna con una pregunta.

choices.text: To get the head teacher to state exactly how many Saturdays remain.
To show that nobody in the school cared about the library any more.
To make everyone consider the problem before she gave any figures.

feedback.es: La pregunta no espera respuesta («nobody needed to»): prepara al público para reflexionar antes de recibir los datos.

origin.audio: Yesterday a student spoke to the whole school and asked, how many more Saturdays must this library stay closed? Nobody answered, and nobody needed to. She then listed what had been lost: fewer books, fewer computers, fewer hours. The head teacher listened carefully, nodded once, and said only that the budget was a matter for the council, which is why some students left the hall doubtful.

prompt.es: Lee el extracto. ¿Qué actitud transmite la oradora hacia la decisión del ayuntamiento?

choices.text: She questions the decision by setting an official word against a child's experience.
She accepts the decision but asks the council to explain how much it saves.
She praises the council for listening to what the youngest pupils think.

feedback.es: Opone el término oficial («a saving») a la vivencia de un niño («the day the lights went out»): cuestiona la decisión con un contraste emotivo.

origin.text: “The council calls this a saving. The children call it a loss. One of them, only nine years old, calls it something simpler: the day the lights went out.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Los alumnos se negaron a permanecer callados.»

feedback.es: Remain silent es la colocación para «permanecer callado»: remain va seguido del adjetivo, no de un adverbio.

origin.text: When the council cut the opening hours, the students could have kept quiet. Instead, they refused to remain ___, and the next morning every door of the school had a note from a pupil.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del discurso con el recurso que emplea.

pairs: Who will listen if we all stay silent?
Fewer books, fewer computers, fewer hours.
The bell is a lantern for lost children.

feedback.es: Una pregunta sin respuesta, el mismo comienzo repetido y una imagen concreta son recursos distintos.

pairs: Who will listen if we all stay silent?
Fewer books, fewer computers, fewer hours.
The bell is a lantern for lost children.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué fin cierra el orador con la última frase.

choices.text: To admit that a library is an old idea that has failed.
To persuade the audience that a library is still worth defending.
To warn the audience that reading rooms will soon be noisy.

feedback.es: Responde a quienes llaman a la biblioteca una idea vieja y le da la vuelta: es lo más nuevo que tenemos. Busca convencer de que merece defenderse.

origin.audio: The next speaker was less gentle. You have heard the figures, he said. You have heard the promises. Now hear the silence of an empty reading room. Some will say a library is an old idea; I say it is the newest place we have, because it asks for nothing except your attention.

prompt.es: Completa: «No eres solo oyente: eres quien puede cambiar esto.»

feedback.es: Belong to the cause describe el efecto de la apelación directa: cada oyente se siente parte del mensaje.

origin.text: You are not just a listener; you are the one who can change this. By speaking directly to the audience, the speaker makes every person feel that they ___ to the cause.

prompt.es: Ordena el fragmento con repetición: «No retrocederemos; no nos rendiremos.»

answer.text: We will not step back, we will not give up

feedback.es: Repetir we will not al inicio de cada parte crea ritmo y firmeza.

title.es: Nunca antes y lo que más importa

es: Usar oraciones cleft, inversión y do enfático para dar énfasis a las ideas clave de un discurso por una causa.

vocabulary.es: concienciar, dar a conocer un problema

teaching.en: What this river needs is not another promise from the council but a hundred volunteers with gloves and a free Saturday.
teaching.es: Lo que este río necesita no es otra promesa del ayuntamiento, sino cien voluntarios con guantes y un sábado libre.
teaching.explanationEs: Cleft con what: What + sujeto + verbo + is + la idea que destacas.
segments: What this river needs is not another promise from the council
but a hundred volunteers with gloves and a free Saturday.
teaching.audioText: What this river needs is not another promise from the council but a hundred volunteers with gloves and a free Saturday.

teaching.en: It is our children, not the politicians, who will pay for this litter when the river floods again next winter.
teaching.es: Son nuestros hijos, no los políticos, quienes pagarán por esta basura cuando el río se desborde otra vez el próximo invierno.
teaching.explanationEs: It is + idea destacada + who/that: pone el foco en quién o qué, y contrasta con not.
segments: It is our children, not the politicians, who will pay
for this litter when the river floods again next winter.
teaching.audioText: It is our children, not the politicians, who will pay for this litter when the river floods again next winter.

teaching.en: Never before have so many neighbours joined a clean-up, and never before has the river been so close to recovery.
teaching.es: Nunca antes se habían sumado tantos vecinos a una limpieza, y nunca antes había estado el río tan cerca de recuperarse.
teaching.explanationEs: Never before al inicio: el auxiliar (have/has) va antes del sujeto.
segments: Never before have so many neighbours joined a clean-up, and
never before has the river been so close to recovery.
teaching.audioText: Never before have so many neighbours joined a clean-up, and never before has the river been so close to recovery.

teaching.en: Not only is the water dangerous to swim in, but under no circumstances should children play on the banks after heavy rain.
teaching.es: El agua no solo es peligrosa para nadar, sino que en ningún caso deben jugar los niños en las orillas tras una lluvia fuerte.
teaching.explanationEs: Not only y under no circumstances al inicio: is y should van antes del sujeto.
segments: Not only is the water dangerous to swim in, but under
no circumstances should children play on the banks after heavy rain.
teaching.audioText: Not only is the water dangerous to swim in, but under no circumstances should children play on the banks after heavy rain.

teaching.en: We do care about this river, and we do want answers from everyone who ignored the flood warnings last spring.
teaching.es: Sí nos importa este río, y sí queremos respuestas de todos los que ignoraron las alertas de inundación la primavera pasada.
teaching.explanationEs: Do + verbo base: el do enfático afirma con fuerza; con he/she es does y en pasado did.
segments: We do care about this river, and we do want
answers from everyone who ignored the flood warnings last spring.
teaching.audioText: We do care about this river, and we do want answers from everyone who ignored the flood warnings last spring.

teaching.en: Only when the water is clean will our children swim here; until then, we will keep working to raise awareness.
teaching.es: Solo cuando el agua esté limpia nadarán aquí nuestros hijos; hasta entonces, seguiremos trabajando para concienciar a la gente.
teaching.explanationEs: Only when al inicio: en la segunda parte el auxiliar will va antes del sujeto.
segments: Only when the water is clean will our children swim
here; until then, we will keep working to raise awareness.
teaching.audioText: Only when the water is clean will our children swim here; until then, we will keep working to raise awareness.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nunca antes había visto nuestra ciudad una inundación así.»

feedback.es: Con never before el auxiliar va antes del sujeto: has our town seen, con el sujeto en tercera persona.

hint.es: Tras «never before» viene primero el auxiliar; el sujeto our town es de tercera persona.

origin.text: It was not one bad night; it was three weeks of rain, and the town was not ready. Never before ___ our town seen such a flood.

prompt.es: Elige la versión con cleft que destaca el agua limpia sin cambiar el sentido.

choices.text: What we need is clean water, not more promises.
It is clean water what we need, not more promises.
What is clean water we need, not more promises.

feedback.es: El cleft con what lleva what + sujeto + verbo + is + la idea destacada; las otras versiones desordenan sus piezas.

hint.es: El cleft empieza con What + sujeto + verbo y luego va is.

origin.text: Base sentence: We need clean water, not more promises. The council has promised a lot; what we lack is the water itself.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Solo cuando actuemos juntos se recuperará el río.»

answer.text: Only when we act together will the river recover

feedback.es: Tras only when, la segunda parte invierte el auxiliar: will the river recover.

hint.es: El auxiliar will va antes de the river.

prompt.es: Reescribe con inversión la última frase de la carta al periódico.

choices.text: Rarely the mayor does listen to us.
Rarely does the mayor listen to us.
Rarely does the mayor listens to us.

feedback.es: Tras el adverbio rarely al inicio hace falta does + sujeto + verbo en forma base.

origin.text: Letter to the editor: For months we have written to the mayor, and she has not replied once. The mayor rarely listens to us, and the flood showed the cost of that silence.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ella sí que ama este río; por eso lo limpia cada semana.»

feedback.es: El do enfático con she es does, y el verbo siguiente queda en forma base.

origin.text: People say the young do not care. That is simply wrong: they spend every weekend by the water, and one girl more than anyone ___ love this river, which is why she cleans it every week.

prompt.es: Destaca «your help» con It is … that, sin cambiar el sentido.

answer.text: It is your help that we need.
accepted: It is your help that we need.
It's your help that we need.
It is your help we need.
It is your help which we need.

feedback.es: El cleft con it is coloca la idea destacada entre it is y that.

origin.text: Flyer draft: We have the gloves and the bags, and the river is waiting. We need your help. Nothing else is missing.

prompt.es: Escucha el discurso y elige qué deja entender la oradora sobre el ayuntamiento.

choices.text: It has answered every petition but has ignored the volunteers.
It wants to keep the river clean but lacks the funds for it.
It talks a lot but has rarely turned its words into action.

feedback.es: «Rarely has the council answered one» y «only when it leads to action will we believe in it» dan a entender que el ayuntamiento habla mucho y actúa poco.

origin.audio: Good evening, everyone. I will keep this short. What this river needs is not another meeting but a real plan. Never before have so many neighbours signed a petition, and rarely has the council answered one. We do want a dialogue, but only when it leads to action will we believe in it. Until then, it is the volunteers, not the politicians, who will keep this river alive, and we will not stop asking for answers.

prompt.es: Ordena: «No solo nos ignoraron, sino que además nos cerraron la puerta.»

answer.text: Not only did they ignore us, they also closed the door
accepted: Not only did they ignore us, they also closed the door
Not only did they ignore us, but they also closed the door

feedback.es: Con not only al inicio el pasado lleva did antes del sujeto y el verbo en forma base.

prompt.es: Reescribe con What … is para destacar «answers».

feedback.es: El cleft con what pone la idea destacada al final, después de is.

origin.text: Statement to the press: We are not asking for money or for a photo with the mayor. We want answers. We want them this week.

prompt.es: Lee el correo. ¿Qué actitud deja entrever el ayuntamiento?

choices.text: It sounds friendly but promises no action before the review ends.
It refuses to discuss the river and rejects the concern completely.
It backs the volunteers' plan and announces a date for the works.

feedback.es: Muestra buena voluntad («we do appreciate»), pero condiciona cualquier obra a que termine la revisión del presupuesto: amable de palabra, sin compromisos.

origin.text: Email from the council: “We do appreciate your concern, and we do plan to respond. Only when the budget review is complete will we be able to confirm any works. Under no circumstances should volunteers enter the water before that date.”

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige qué da a entender sobre la voluntaria.

choices.text: She is proud that many neighbours stay until the end of each cleaning.
She is tired of depending on so few people but keeps asking for help.
She has stopped asking for help because nobody ever answers her.

feedback.es: Dice que son siempre los mismos los que se quedan y que, aun así, pide una ayuda más cada sábado: cansancio sin rendirse.

origin.audio: This week we meet a volunteer who has cleaned the same stretch of river for six years. She says it is not the litter that worries her but the silence around it. Little did she expect so many neighbours to join her, and yet it is always the same few who stay until the end. Rarely does she complain, but she does ask, every single Saturday, for one more pair of hands.

prompt.es: Completa: «Son los jóvenes quienes limpiarán este río el año próximo.»

feedback.es: En it-cleft, el sujeto que se destaca va seguido de who (personas) o that.

origin.text: The council promised much and delivered little. It is the young people ___ will clean this river next year, and it is the neighbours who will keep it clean.

prompt.es: Elige la frase con inversión correcta para abrir el párrafo de Mia.

choices.text: Rarely does the council answers our letters.
Rarely the council does answer our letters.
Rarely does the council answer our letters.

feedback.es: Con rarely al inicio se invierte el auxiliar do y el verbo principal queda en forma base: does … answer.

origin.text: Mia's notes: The council answers our letters about once a year, and the floods come every winter. She wants the next paragraph to open with “Rarely” to stress how often the council stays silent.

es: Distinguir argumentos legítimos de falacias y presiones emocionales en anuncios y discursos, y justificar el veredicto.

teaching.en: Everyone is buying it, so you should too; that is the bandwagon, and popularity alone is never proof that something is good.
teaching.es: Todo el mundo lo compra, así que tú también deberías; eso es el bandwagon, y la popularidad por sí sola nunca prueba que algo sea bueno.
teaching.explanationEs: Bandwagon: usa lo que hace la mayoría como única razón; no ofrece pruebas.
segments: Everyone is buying it, so you should too; that is the
bandwagon, and popularity alone is never proof that something is good.
teaching.audioText: Everyone is buying it, so you should too; that is the bandwagon, and popularity alone is never proof that something is good.

teaching.en: Hurry! Only two tickets are left and the price rises at midnight: this ad creates false urgency so that you decide without thinking.
teaching.es: ¡Date prisa! Solo quedan dos entradas y el precio sube a medianoche: este anuncio crea una falsa urgencia para que decidas sin pensar.
teaching.explanationEs: Falsa urgencia: presiona para decidir rápido, aunque no haya ningún motivo real para la prisa.
segments: Hurry! Only two tickets are left and the price rises at midnight:
this ad creates false urgency so that you decide without thinking.
teaching.audioText: Hurry! Only two tickets are left and the price rises at midnight: this ad creates false urgency so that you decide without thinking.

teaching.en: Either we build the car park or the shop will close, but a false dilemma hides the other options that an honest speaker would mention.
teaching.es: O construimos el aparcamiento o la tienda cerrará, pero un falso dilema oculta las otras opciones que un orador honesto mencionaría.
teaching.explanationEs: False dilemma: presenta solo dos opciones cuando hay más; either… or suele delatarlo.
segments: Either we build the car park or the shop will close, but a
false dilemma hides the other options that an honest speaker would mention.
teaching.audioText: Either we build the car park or the shop will close, but a false dilemma hides the other options that an honest speaker would mention.

teaching.en: A survey of four hundred families found that seventy per cent want a safe crossing, which is legitimate evidence because anyone can check the figures.
teaching.es: Una encuesta a cuatrocientas familias halló que el setenta por ciento quiere un paso de peatones seguro, lo cual es una prueba legítima porque cualquiera puede comprobar las cifras.
teaching.explanationEs: Evidencia legítima: dato concreto, con fuente y cifra que se puede verificar.
segments: A survey of four hundred families found that seventy per cent want a
safe crossing, which is legitimate evidence because anyone can check the figures.
teaching.audioText: A survey of four hundred families found that seventy per cent want a safe crossing, which is legitimate evidence because anyone can check the figures.

teaching.en: Our famous singer uses this shampoo, so it must be the best, but being famous says nothing about what is inside the bottle.
teaching.es: Nuestra cantante famosa usa este champú, así que debe de ser el mejor, pero ser famosa no dice nada de lo que hay dentro del frasco.
teaching.explanationEs: Falacia de autoridad: la fama no da autoridad sobre un tema que no es el suyo.
segments: Our famous singer uses this shampoo, so it must be the best,
but being famous says nothing about what is inside the bottle.
teaching.audioText: Our famous singer uses this shampoo, so it must be the best, but being famous says nothing about what is inside the bottle.

teaching.en: Think of your own child at the crossing every morning: a feeling tied to a real risk is fair, but fear without facts is misleading.
teaching.es: Piensa en tu propio hijo en el paso de peatones cada mañana: un sentimiento ligado a un riesgo real es justo, pero el miedo sin datos es engañoso.
teaching.explanationEs: La emoción legítima se apoya en un riesgo real; sin hechos, es presión y resulta engañosa.
segments: Think of your own child at the crossing every morning: a feeling tied
to a real risk is fair, but fear without facts is misleading.
teaching.audioText: Think of your own child at the crossing every morning: a feeling tied to a real risk is fair, but fear without facts is misleading.

prompt.es: Valora el anuncio: ¿es legítimo o engañoso y por qué?

choices.text: Legitimate: it gives a clear deadline that helps buyers choose fairly.
Misleading: it adds pressure and popularity but gives no real reason.
Legitimate: it shows that many people have tested the shoes properly.

feedback.es: Mezcla falsa urgencia (quedan dos, acaba esta noche) y bandwagon (todos las llevan), pero no da ninguna razón sobre la calidad del producto.

hint.es: Busca si el anuncio da una razón sobre el producto o solo prisa y popularidad.

origin.text: Ad: “Buy now! Only two pairs left, and the offer ends tonight. Everyone at the gym is already wearing these shoes.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Ofrecer solo dos opciones cuando hay más es un falso dilema.»

feedback.es: False dilemma es la falacia que presenta solo dos salidas y oculta otras posibles, como el día de mercado que propone la alcaldesa.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que sigue a «false» y nombra la falacia de las dos únicas opciones.

origin.text: The speaker said: “Either we build the car park or the shop will close.” The mayor replied that there were other options, such as a market day. Offering only two choices when more exist is a false ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una encuesta a cuatrocientas familias apoya el plan del paso de peatones.»

answer.text: A survey of four hundred families supports the plan for a crossing

feedback.es: La evidencia legítima se construye con una fuente (a survey), una cifra (four hundred families) y lo que apoya.

hint.es: Empieza con A survey y termina con a crossing.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada técnica con su explicación.

pairs: bandwagon

pairs.es: dice que todos lo hacen para convencerte

pairs: false dilemma

pairs.es: finge que solo hay dos opciones

pairs: false urgency

pairs.es: mete prisa sin una razón real

prompt.es: Escucha el discurso y decide qué tipo de apelación es.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje y elige qué técnicas de presión combina el orador.

origin.audio: A local shop has launched a new campaign: choose us, or watch your street disappear. The owner says she is only being honest. Yet the flyers never mention prices, reviews or any other shop in the area. They show only a clock counting down outside the door and a photo of a famous footballer who once walked past the door. One customer said she felt rushed, although nobody had told her anything false, and another said she had bought a coat she did not really need, simply because the clock was running.

answer.text: Imagine a vacant lot turning into a garden full of life. Right now, it grows litter, not vegetables. According to our survey, 120 families would visit it weekly, and every one of them wants to help. What we need is a tight budget, a few tools and forty volunteers. Never before has our neighbourhood had such a chance to grow together. Who will plant the first seed if we do not? It is our children who will eat the vegetables, and it is our neighbours who will share the harvest. Some people see an empty lot; we see a garden. We are not asking for a fortune; we are asking for a few Saturdays. Every signature is a neighbour who is ready to help, and together we can rally support for this garden. So please do not wait. Sign the petition at the school door before Friday, and next summer we will share the first harvest together.

Se necesitan 40 voluntarios y herramientas, con un presupuesto ajustado. La petición se firma en la puerta de la escuela antes del viernes. Incluye gancho, dato, tres recursos de énfasis y una petición clara.

origin.text: The council will not move without pressure from the neighbourhood. To ___ support for the garden, Sara is collecting signatures at the school door every afternoon this week.

origin.audio: Nobody wanted to live next to an empty lot. Now forty families are asking for a garden, and the council has said it would like to help, although it cannot promise a budget before June. Some of you have told me you are too busy, and I understand that; but nobody here has less time than the children who are waiting. If we wait for the council alone, the land will stay empty for another year. So I will ask you one thing tonight: will you help them? Will you be the first to sign?

origin.text: “We are not asking for a fortune; we are asking for a few Saturdays.” The speaker says this just before she asks the audience to sign the petition.

es: Defender una causa local ante un público y responder a una objeción con respeto, evidencia y una petición final.

vocabulary.es: hacer una pausa para dar fuerza
admitir que el otro tiene razón en algo

teaching.en: Let me be clear: a crossing is not a luxury, it is a need, and we have the figures to prove it.
teaching.es: Seré claro: un paso de peatones no es un lujo, es una necesidad, y tenemos las cifras para demostrarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Let me be clear introduce la idea central con firmeza; combina bien con un contraste (not… it is).
segments: Let me be clear: a crossing is not a luxury, it
is a need, and we have the figures to prove it.
teaching.audioText: Let me be clear: a crossing is not a luxury, it is a need, and we have the figures to prove it.

teaching.en: I want to address a concern raised by some neighbours: the delay to the traffic would last two minutes, no more.
teaching.es: Quiero atender una preocupación planteada por algunos vecinos: la demora en el tráfico duraría dos minutos, no más.
teaching.explanationEs: Address a concern: nombra la objeción con respeto antes de responderla con un dato.
segments: I want to address a concern raised by some neighbours: the
delay to the traffic would last two minutes, no more.
teaching.audioText: I want to address a concern raised by some neighbours: the delay to the traffic would last two minutes, no more.

teaching.en: That is a fair point, and I am willing to concede it: a crossing will cost money, but one accident would cost far more.
teaching.es: Es un punto razonable y estoy dispuesto a admitirlo: un paso de peatones costará dinero, pero un accidente costaría mucho más.
teaching.explanationEs: Concede a point: admitir lo cierto da credibilidad; luego vuelve a tu argumento con but o however.
segments: That is a fair point, and I am willing to concede it:

teaching.audioText: That is a fair point, and I am willing to concede it: a crossing will cost money, but one accident would cost far more.

prompt.es: Escribe tu discurso por el paso de peatones y responde a dos objeciones.

answer.text: Who will speak for a child who cannot vote? This year, three children almost had an accident at our school gate. What we need is a safe crossing. Our survey is clear: 82% of families support it. Some of you may say it will cost too much. I understand your concern, but one accident would cost far more. Others say it will cause a delay to the traffic. That is a fair point; however, two minutes of delay is nothing next to a child's safety. Never before have so many parents asked for something so simple. It is our children who cross that road every morning, and it is we who must protect them. Let me be clear: a crossing is not a luxury, it is a need. I do not ask you for a favour; I ask you for what every child in this town deserves, and I ask you to stand with me tonight. So please sign the petition before Friday, because our children cannot wait.

Imagine a child crossing our road every morning. Three of them almost had an accident this year. A survey found that 82% of families want a safe crossing. I understand the concern about the cost, but one accident would cost much more. It is true that the traffic will slow down; however, two minutes of delay is nothing next to a life. What we need is action, and never before have so many parents asked for it. It is our children who cross that road every morning, and it is we who must protect them. Despite the delay, children will be safer, and the survey shows that families agree. Let me be clear: we will not stop asking. Please sign the petition before Friday.

feedback.es: El discurso completo lleva gancho, dato de la encuesta, énfasis, respuesta a las dos objeciones y una petición con fecha.

origin.text: Datos: paso de peatones seguro frente a la escuela. Este año, tres niños casi fueron atropellados. Una encuesta halló que el 82 % de las familias lo apoya. Objeciones: «cuesta demasiado» y «retrasará el tráfico». Petición final: firmar la petición antes del viernes. Incluye gancho, dato, dos recursos de énfasis, respuesta a las dos objeciones y una petición final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la oradora empieza respondiendo con «I hear that concern».

choices.text: To avoid the question by changing the subject to the survey.
To admit that the crossing is a waste of the council's money.
To show respect for the objection before answering it with evidence.

feedback.es: Reconocer la objeción («I hear that concern») antes de responder con la encuesta muestra respeto y da credibilidad a su postura.

origin.audio: A question came from the back of the hall: is a crossing not a waste of public money? The speaker took a breath and paused. Nobody moved, and she did not raise her voice once. I hear that concern, she said, and I will not pretend that money is no object. But the survey is clear: eighty-two per cent of parents feel afraid at the gate, and three children were almost hurt there this year. So please sign before Friday.

prompt.es: Completa: «Di la frase clave despacio y haz una pausa antes de la última palabra.»

feedback.es: Slowly es el adverbio que describe cómo decir la frase clave: despacio, para que el público la asimile.

origin.text: Good speakers do not rush their most important sentence. They say the key line ___ and pause for effect before the last word.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que usa despite correctamente.

choices.text: Despite the delay, children will be safer.
Despite of the delay, children will be safer.
In spite the delay, children will be safer.

feedback.es: Despite va seguido directamente del sustantivo: despite the delay. Despite of es un error, y in spite necesita of (in spite of).

origin.text: Carlos wants to say that, even though the crossing will cause a short delay, children will be safer. He is not sure which word must come next.
